authorization: Maintainer instruction 2026-09-17: convert the Codex QA skill at src/agents/skills/qa into a Claude Code skill at src/claude/skills named qa. Authorizes writing the converted package into the selected target_root only; no installation, host configuration, hook or settings registration, mirroring into .claude/, product execution, testing or validation.

requirements.outcome: The Codex qa package is converted to a Claude Code skill at src/claude/skills/qa, preserving its independent specification-driven QA contract: mode selection, plan publication, integrity inspection, execution, stop control, metric floors, reporting and the dev remediation handoff.

Every one of the nine source files carries an explicit disposition. Eight are preserved or rewritten into the target and one, agents/openai.yaml, is omitted with its substantive content relocated; no file is silently dropped.

The two reference files with no host-specific content, references/assessment.md and references/execution-integrity.md, are preserved byte-for-byte. Their mentions of MCP and browser access describe host-independence and remain true on Claude Code, so they are not transformed.

Codex host mechanics are mapped to Claude Code: the cold-session statement names Claude Code, and the five handoff lines that tell the user to open or paste into a Codex conversation name the Claude Code session instead. Host metadata lives entirely in SKILL.md frontmatter because Claude Code has no separate metadata file, so agents/openai.yaml is dropped rather than ported.

The openai.yaml interface block is resolved field by field: display_name 'Independent QA' and short_description 'Plan and run independent specification-driven QA' are folded into the frontmatter name and description, and default_prompt with its $qa substitution syntax is recorded as unreproduced source metadata rather than held in an invented frontmatter key.

allowed-tools is derived from the declared capabilities and makes two asserted source boundaries structural: Skill is omitted so the workflow cannot auto-send the dev handoff or invoke the package validator it defers to, and Task is omitted as the minimum grant.

AskUserQuestion is named at the three bounded decision points the source could only express as prose: an ungroundable evidence destination, an essential unresolved choice or additional permission after discovery, and an unresolved choice that changes the assessment.

The Codex-era instruction to verify namespaced plugin syntax with 'no assumed Claude-style namespace' is rewritten rather than deleted: the underlying requirement, that dev availability is observed rather than assumed, is preserved and mapped to the session's actual available-skills list on this host.

The body states plainly that unscoped Bash does not enforce the prohibitions the skill carries, so no-product-repair, no-installation, no-deployment and the mock-decorator prohibition are recorded as contract obligations rather than implied allowlist enforcement.
The package remains portable: no installation root, repository-specific path, operator path or fixed evidence directory is wired into any converted file.

capabilities: Claude Code file tools (Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep) for inspecting the candidate and writing QA plans, reports, fix packets and evidence records
Unscoped Bash, because the authored skill derives build, test, coverage and static-analysis commands from runtime project inputs and no command-name pattern can be fixed in advance
AskUserQuestion for bounded decisions with known options
expected_outputs: Converted Claude Code skill package at the target root, comprising SKILL.md, four references and three asset templates
side_effects: The authored skill, when later run by a user, creates isolated QA-owned fixtures and harnesses, runs local builds, tests and instrumentation, and writes plan, report, fix-packet, checkpoint and manifest files inside the selected evidence destination
known_issues: No bound Python evaluation artifacts were created for this package: no evals/, tests/ or scripts/ directory exists. AGENTS.md names such artifacts required for a skill build, and the source package's own QA-026 / QAP-014 clause states that qa's evaluated-build completeness requires exactly such a bundle. skill-builder forbids generating evaluation campaigns during authoring and the validator package is documented as owning all quality campaigns. Recorded as design open question Q1 for the maintainer; the conversion did not resolve it.

Task is omitted from allowed-tools, so QA independence from development completion claims remains a contract obligation of the single session rather than a fresh-context boundary the host enforces. Recorded as design open question Q2.
The >=95% coverage and unit-test pass-rate floors are preserved as written in references/assessment.md rather than converted into project-policy inputs. Recorded as design open question Q3.

Only the selected target_root is written. The ADR-073 mirror at .claude/skills/qa is not created by this run, matching the dev conversion whose authoring record shows its .claude/ copy was made outside the run. Recorded as design open question Q4 and reported as a separate pending action.

Unscoped Bash is granted. The skill's prohibitions on product repair, installation, deployment and persistent startup changes are contract obligations that the allowlist does not enforce; the SKILL.md body states this rather than implying enforcement.
Validation and testing are NOT_PERFORMED for the converted bytes.

The two prior runs under docs/plan/skill-authorings/qa/ (20260914T1748018341005Z and 20260914T193851Z) were inspected before staging: both bind target_root C:\Projects\DevForgeAI\src\agents\skills\qa with operation edit, which is the Codex source package and a different target_root from this Claude target. They are authoring history for the source, not for this destination, and no run under this target_root exists, so history_review is no_known_history. Those runs remain in place as append-only evidence.
